fec._leadersNote: leaders.<chamber> lists the party leaders whose committees' money build_establishment.py totals per cycle (chamber = member.chamber). 'numKey' exposes a leader's all-cycle total to establishment_items.json as {dccc} or {dscc}. leadershipRx/leadershipIds drive the Money page's single-leader box: House 'JEFFRIES|JEFF PAC'; Senate 'SCHUMER|^IMPACT$' with leadershipIds ["C00346312", "C00348607"].

profile._note: Curated page text, rendered by the pages at runtime. Strings allow [label](url), **bold** and {{tokens}} (e.g. {{short}}, {{poss}}). Every fact typed here also goes in data/claims_static.json with its source.
profile.lede: A running check of what {{short}} promised San Fernando Valley voters, what she has done in office, and what she says on the issues people are fighting about. Every entry links to its source.

facts.label: Background
facts.value: Electrical engineer; founded DIY Girls; six years in the State Assembly

facts.label: 2026 general
facts.value: Re-elected 57.3% to 42.7% over fellow Democrat Angélica María Dueñas, unofficial, all 115 precincts reporting

facts.label: 2024 general
facts.value: Won an open seat 69.8% to 30.2% over Benito Bernal (R)

factSources: Committees: [House Clerk member data, Nov 3, 2026](https://clerk.house.gov/xml/lists/MemberData.xml). Background: [her campaign site](https://www.luzforcongress.com/about).
2026 general (unofficial, all 115 precincts reporting): Rivas 100,242 (57.3%), Dueñas 74,798 (42.7%). [CA Secretary of State](https://api.sos.ca.gov/returns/us-rep/district/29)
2024 general (certified): Rivas 146,312 (69.8%), Bernal 63,374 (30.2%). [CA Secretary of State, Statement of Vote](https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/sov/2024-general/sov/25-us-rep-congress.pdf)

committees.name: Natural Resources Committee
committees.blurb: Oversees federal public lands, water, and energy and mineral development. Her office says these panels "play key roles in addressing the climate crisis" and in preserving public lands and water. [Source](https://rivas.house.gov/media/press-releases/congresswoman-rivas-named-key-natural-resources-subcommittees-address-climate)

committees.name: Science, Space, and Technology Committee
committees.blurb: Oversees federal science agencies and research programs. Her office ties it to clean energy, STEM education and AI oversight. [Source](https://rivas.house.gov/media/press-releases/congresswoman-luz-rivas-selected-key-panels-house-committee-science-space-and)

House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC)
profile.promisesIntro: Each 2024 campaign promise set against her bills, votes and district work. Her campaign site had no issues page, so the explicit promises come from her own words on that site and in her candidacy announcement. Two more are themes of the record she ran on, labeled as such. "Stalled" means she acted but the outcome didn't move her way or her bill hasn't advanced. Statuses are this tracker's judgment; each says what it rests on.

map.heading: CA-29 is mostly the northeast San Fernando Valley
map.intro: Nearly everyone in the district lives in the City of Los Angeles, in communities like Pacoima, Sylmar, Panorama City and Van Nuys; the rest live in the City of San Fernando. Prop 50 redrew the lines for the 2026 election. The new map takes effect Jan 3, 2027; until then she represents the 2023 lines.
map.note: Shaded areas are the parts of each community inside the district; the dark line is the district boundary. Shares are by land area, not population; slivers under 5% are left out as boundary-file mismatches. Communities: [LA County Countywide Statistical Areas](https://egis-lacounty.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/countywide-statistical-areas-csa) (LA County Enterprise GIS). District lines: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb (119th and 120th Congressional Districts). Population: 2020 Census, from the [California Senate Office of Demographics](https://sdmg.senate.ca.gov/committeehome/2025-congressional-districts/congressional-district-29-2025). Her campaign site lists 16 communities in the district, all of which appear here.

money.watchIntro: Her constituents care most about immigration enforcement, housing and the cost of living, public safety and homelessness. These groups total the PACs and donor employers whose names fit each category.
money.trackaipacNote: Track AIPAC is also listed among the 2026 endorsers of her general-election opponent, Angélica María Dueñas ([Dueñas campaign site](https://angelica4congress.com/endorsements/)).

events.intro: Public events from her press releases and local news. Her office's [events page](https://rivas.house.gov/about/events) lists no upcoming events.
events.help: Her office also posts help pages on [immigrants' rights](https://rivas.house.gov/services/know-your-rights), [DACA renewal](https://rivas.house.gov/services/daca-renewal-resources-and-faqs) and [help with a federal agency](https://rivas.house.gov/services/help-federal-agency).
events.ask: Her office does not post upcoming events online. Call the district office to ask, or see every way to reach her on the [Overview](./#channels).

overview._note: Member-specific Overview tiles (scripts/build_overview.py). costPromise: start of the promise 'issue' in data/promises.json whose status answers 'Delivering on cost of living?'; costPledge: how the tile names that pledge (default 'cost-of-living'). themes may add a 'note' after the rule. themes: [{q, rx, section, noun}] counts press releases mentioning a topic (e.g. Luz Rivas: Focused on homelessness?). votes: [{q, roll, section, what}] shows one recorded vote (e.g. the Epstein Files Transparency Act, House roll 2025-289).

themes.note: One funded project and one bill.
